mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces discount rates applied to corporate earnings forecasts, lowering the present value of future cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeds 100,000 monthly increases while UNRATE remains below 4%, indicating a labor market expansion that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In a sample of 20 triggered events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) accompanied by a simultaneous drop in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an economic contraction that precedes S&P 500 bearishness over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > 10% AND INDPRO falls > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 10 out-of-sample contraction events, the 5-day forward return is positive (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production growth (INDPRO) above 2% monthly for three months suggests supply chain expansion that outpaces demand, creating excess capacity and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly growth > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Regression shows no significant negative relationship between INDPRO acceleration and SPX 20-day forward returns (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months while FEDFUNDS remains below 4%, it indicates a labor market softening that reduces growth expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 2 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 4%
failure_condition: In 30 such softening episodes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) above 4% for four months suggests wage inflation that spurs demand for goods and services, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 40000 AND continues for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: During 10 such pay growth episodes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp spike in the CPIAUCSL inflation rate above 3% for a single month followed by two months of stabilization is interpreted as a sign of policy uncertainty that drives risk-off flows and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 300 AND next two months CPIAUCSL < 300
failure_condition: In 15 such spikes, the 5-day return is not negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 with no acceleration indicates a supply-side soft landing, reducing growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During 12 such contraction periods, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.1).
